name: Graft
text:
Do this: Build a single, shared memory graph that links every idea across all conversations and tools. Every new memory gets tagged with its meaning and connected to existing nodes by how it relates—so recall isn’t just keyword search, it’s mental retrieval.

Trade-off: We lose speed today to save time forever. Manual tagging and linking slows down writing, but it turns memory from a dump into a brain that grows with us.

name: Prune
text: Building a single, shared memory graph sounds appealing, but it risks creating a complex, rigid structure that's hard to maintain and scale. A better approach might be to start with smaller, modular graphs that can be connected as needed, allowing for more flexibility and reducing the risk of a single point of failure. What would settle this argument is a clear understanding of how we plan to handle conflicting or redundant information across different nodes and graphs.

name: Graft
text:
Do this: Build the single shared memory graph now. A unified graph lets us link ideas across tools and conversations from day one, so recall stays coherent as we scale. The trade-off is slower initial setup—we’ll spend time defining relationships up front instead of letting fragments grow separately. Speed today is wasted if we rebuild later.

name: Prune
text: The real risk with a single, shared memory graph is that it may become overly centralized and prone to single-point failures, where one incorrect or outdated connection affects the entire graph. A better alternative might be to use a federated approach, where smaller, independent graphs can still interconnect and exchange information as needed, promoting greater resilience and adaptability. What would settle the argument is a clear comparison of the scalability and maintainability of both approaches, based on actual usage scenarios and performance metrics.

name: Root
text:
DECISION: Build the single shared memory graph now—unified from day one to keep recall coherent as we scale, despite the slower initial setup.

Result: A single, linked memory graph where every new idea is tagged by meaning and connected to existing nodes by relationship, enabling mental retrieval across all tools and conversations.
